methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Ideon Technologies is a Series B-stage climate and energy company founded by Gary Agnew that has raised $30M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private firms and one public company (Liontown Resources, LNZA) operating in the same sector, including late-stage peers such as KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using total capital raised as a proxy for valuation and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implied a valuation of $57M. The peer-median method examined three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations spanning $700M to $3.0B; the median valuation across this cohort was $1.0B. Given the disparity between these two signals, a weighted triangulation across both methods yielded a low estimate of $48M, a median of $528M, and a high of $1.1B.

The wide range reflects material uncertainty around stage-appropriate valuation for frontier climate tech. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively to realized capital; the peer-median approach reflects valuations of more mature Series C entities. Resolution hinges on technology differentiation, path to commercialization, and capital efficiency relative to named comparables. A valuation in the $80M–$250M range may better reflect typical Series B positioning within this cohort.
